summary: SLA enforcement bypass when macro-based priority override exists
description:
Issue summary: After last week's rule-engine (v2.7.1) rollout, certain tickets that hit SLA thresholds are not being escalated to on-call when a macro-based priority override is applied.

Impact: Internal routing and on-call notification gaps for high-severity incidents. Multiple internal alerts were not escalated, delaying triage by ~45-90 minutes in two observed occurrences. This affects Redwood internal support workflows (no customer-facing incidents observed yet) and risks missing external-facing escalations if similar logic applies to customer routes.

Observed behavior: When an automation macro ("override_priority=urgent") is applied by a templated routing macro, the SLA-enforcement step in the rule pipeline appears to be skipped for that issue object. The issue keeps its original SLA timestamp but does not generate an escalation ticket nor trigger the scheduled webhook to PagerDuty.

Expected behavior: Macro-based priority overrides should not short-circuit SLA enforcement. SLA checks must run after macro expansions and apply escalate/fallback policies accordingly.

Steps to reproduce (prod-like staging repro available):
1) Create a synthetic internal-support issue with priority default P3 and SLA policy set to escalate to on-call after 30m.
2) Apply macro "override_priority=urgent" via the UI or automation API.
3) Observe rule execution trace in Rule Engine logs: the SLA enforcement rule should re-evaluate and schedule escalation. Instead, trace shows evaluation order: macros -> routing -> persist, without re-evaluating SLA conditions.
4) Wait past SLA window and confirm no escalation webhook was emitted (check notifications logs and PagerDuty activity).

Workaround (manual): Manually trigger escalation from the support console or remove macro and re-apply a no-op change which forces re-evaluation. Not acceptable for scale.
investigation_notes:
Initial findings:
- Timeline: First repro on 2026-03-11 09:14 UTC, second on 2026-03-12 02:03 UTC. Both on us-east cluster.
- Correlation with recent deploy: rule-engine v2.7.1 (deployed 2026-03-10) introduced a change to evaluation ordering to optimize macro expansion latency.
- Logs: rule-engine trace shows rules executed in the following order: macro_expander -> routing_selector -> persistence. SLA_enforcer job is scheduled only if SLA_enforcer fires before persistence. In prior versions SLA_enforcer ran after all macro changes and before persistence; new path sometimes schedules SLA check as a background cron tied to original object version.
- Code pointers: parsers in repo support-tooling/rules/engine/main.py altered ordering in commit 3f9a2b4 (PR #405). See related_github_prs.
- Hypothesis: When macro updates mutate the priority field after the SLA check is computed on the object snapshot, SLA_enforcer does not pick up the updated priority because it is referencing a stale object version. The new optimization also defers SLA re-eval in some code paths.
- Impacted modules: macro-expander, rule-evaluator, sla-enforcer scheduler, persistence_hook.

Evidence & links:
- Slack: #support-tooling thread (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C0ABCDEF/p1688581200000)
- Kibana traces: trace IDs: trace-2026-03-11-0914, trace-2026-03-12-0203
- PagerDuty: no trigger for incident IDs that correspond to the support tickets above.

next_steps: 1) Merge hotfix to re-evaluate SLA after macro expansion (PR #419) and deploy to canary routing nodes. 2) Run targeted integration tests and chaos runs for 24h. 3) Monitor rule pipeline p95 and PagerDuty triggers. 4) If stable, promote to full rollout and backfill missed escalations via script.
workarounds: Manual re-trigger via support console or remove/re-apply macros to force rule re-evaluation. Add a temporary monitor to alert when issue with SLA 'escalate' flag is present but no PagerDuty webhook emitted within expected window.
notes_and_followups: Post-fix action items: update runbook to include a check for macro-applied priority overrides, add regression test in CI that asserts SLA re-eval after macro-expansion, and add telemetry to capture 'object version' used by SLA_enforcer for easier debugging in the future. Consider adding a feature flag to revert evaluation-order optimization if needed.
